title: The glowing cloud Sharpless 2-296, part of the Seagull Nebula
caption: Sharpless 2-296 in the Seagull Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: Seagull Nebula · constellation Canis Major · about 3500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Wisps of gas and dust twist through this scene, where dark clouds and glowing red ones weave among bright stars. This is Sharpless 2-296, which makes up part of the wings of the Seagull Nebula.

The red glow comes from hydrogen gas lit up by hot young stars. Their intense light strips electrons from the hydrogen, and as the atoms settle back they shine with a characteristic red color. Regions like this are called H II regions. The dark clouds, by contrast, are cold dust dense enough to block the light behind it.

The Seagull Nebula takes its name from its resemblance to a bird with outstretched wings. The region is a jumble of different kinds of objects packed into one patch of sky. It was taken at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile, using the Wide Field Imager camera mounted on the 2.2-meter MPG/ESO telescope.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.70 x 18.18 arcminutes) and distance (3500 light years), the frame spans roughly 34 × 19 light-years. Its light set out about 3,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope recorded this visible-light image through several broadband filters and a hydrogen-alpha filter. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures and a hydrogen filter bring out faint red gas that the eye would barely register, if at all.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The nebula is about 3,500 light-years away. Its official short catalog name is Sh 2-296, and the Seagull Nebula as a whole has its own formal entry in the IC catalog.
alt: Dark clouds and glowing red clouds of gas and dust winding among bright stars.
